## SECTION 3.5 — SECOND-ORDER EFFECTS & REFLEXIVITY

- **Competitive counter-moves:** Post-close, GTE exits Colombia/Ecuador entirely; Maurel Prom (Pertamina-controlled) consolidates Suroriente + Ecuador positions, strengthening its regional cost curve and potentially tightening the competitive set GTE would have faced in a re-marketing scenario. No counter-move risk on the retained Canada book (different basin, different buyer pool).
- **Pricing tolerance elasticity:** Retained Clearwater realizations carry an ~$8–9/bbl transport/differential drag [Assumption]; at Brent < $65, WCSB cash costs consume >50% of realized price — the asset's pricing power is negative (price-taker with high fixed cost base). Hedges (52% H2-26, floors ≈$60) are the only pricing protection [Actual].
- **Balance sheet reflexivity:** The deal converts a B-rated, 1.5–1.7x leveraged issuer into a debt-free cash shell — this is a one-way ratchet: post-close, GTE can fund buybacks (committed program [Actual]) and EOR capex without dilution or credit-market access risk. Pre-close, every quarter of delay costs ~$10–15M of interest + working-capital drag on the $315M floor [Estimate] — the single most important time-dependence in the thesis.
- **Reflexive flow effect:** The stock has already re-rated from its Oct-2025 low (~$3.09 [Estimate]) to $11.52 on the Aug-5 announcement; special-situations desks will sell into vote-day certainty, which is why entry is tranched below T0 rather than chased (Section 5.5).

- **Bear node (p = 0.25) — two sub-scenarios, internally weighted:**
  - **B1 (60% of node):** Deal closes but Brent collapses to ~$60–65 by 2H27 (Hormuz reopens + OPEC+ spare capacity + recession demand shock). No apocalyptic fiction is required or used; the B2 bankruptcy-adjacent tail is a legitimate 10%-total-probability outcome for a B-rated micro-cap (not an industry oligopolist), grounded in negative tangible equity, not narrative.
